items.title: Definition 9.1.2 (2017: 9.1), branched ep⁺-subgroupoids

book.label: §9.1, Definition 9.1.2, p. 402 (2017: Definition 9.1, p. 292)
book.statement: A branched ep⁺-subgroupoid of the ep-groupoid $X$ is a functor $\Theta : X \to \mathbb Q^+$ with (1) $\mathrm{supp}(\Theta) = \{\Theta > 0\}$ contained in $X_\infty$ and $|\mathrm{supp}(\Theta)|$ paracompact in the topology induced from $|X|$; and, at every $x \in \mathrm{supp}(\Theta)$, (2) an open $U(x)$ and finitely many submanifolds $M_i \subseteq U(x)$ through $x$ with proper inclusions, (3) weights $\sigma_i \in \mathbb Q$, $\sigma_i > 0$, and (4) $\Theta(y) = \sum_{y \in M_i} \sigma_i$ for $y \in U(x)$: a local branching structure.

lean.statement: A branched ep⁺-subgroupoid is a functor $\Theta \ge 0$ whose support lies in the smooth set, whose orbit support $|\mathrm{supp}(\Theta)|$ is paracompact, and which at every $x \in \mathrm{supp}(\Theta)$ has a local branching structure: an open $U(x)$, finitely many smooth submanifolds $M_i \subseteq U(x)$ through $x$ with proper inclusions, weights $\sigma_i > 0$, and $\Theta(y) = \sum_{y \in M_i} \sigma_i$ on $U(x)$. The zero functor and the indicator of a smooth point of $\mathbb R^n$ are examples.

diff: $\Theta$ takes values in $\mathbb Q$ with $\Theta \ge 0$ a field; "the topology induced on $|\mathrm{supp}(\Theta)|$ is paracompact" is a `ParacompactSpace` instance on the subtype; "the inclusion $M_i \to U(x)$ is proper" is `IsProperMap` of the inclusion. The 2017 text's "(ii) and (iii)" in (4) is "(2) and (3)" in 2021 (possible misprint, corrected) (Findings, Chapter 9, item 1). By Remark 9.1.4 the paracompactness is automatic when $|\mathrm{supp}(\Theta)|$ is component compact (`isBranchedEpSubgroupoid_of_isComponentCompact`, V9.63).

items.title: Remark 9.1.1 (2017: 9.1) and the last paragraph of Definition 9.1.2, the dimension of a submanifold and $n$-dimensional $\Theta$

book.label: §9.1, Remark 9.1.1, p. 402 (2017: Remark 9.1, p. 291), and Definition 9.1.2, last paragraph, p. 402
book.statement: The dimension of $T_mM$ is locally constant in $m \in M$, the local dimension of $M$. $\Theta$ is $n$-dimensional if at every point of its support the manifolds of a local branching structure can be taken $n$-dimensional (2017: are $n$-dimensional); by a footnote (new in 2021) an $n$-dimensional $\Theta$ is not $m$-dimensional for $m \ne n$; $\Theta$ is locally equidimensional if small structures have sheets of one dimension.

lean.statement: A submanifold has dimension $k$ at $a$ if the tangent space of its sub-retract at the chart image of $a$ has dimension $k$; the value does not depend on the data and the chart, is unique, exists at every point, and is invariant under restriction to open sets and under sc-diffeomorphisms. It is locally constant on every M-polyfold (`MPolyfold.hasLocallyConstantDimAt`): in a chart it is the rank of $Dt$ for the chart sc⁺-retraction $t$ of the submanifold (`hasDimAt_finrank`), locally constant along the retract (`ScRetraction.eventually_finrank_eq`); so a labelled local branching structure exists at every point of $\mathrm{supp}(\Theta)$ (`hasLabelledBranchingAt_general`). $\Theta$ is $n$-dimensional if at every point of its support some local branching structure has only $n$-dimensional $M_i$; the zero functor is $n$-dimensional for every $n$. The dimensions of the $M_i$ of one structure through $x$ are determined, and at a point of $\mathrm{supp}(\Theta)$ the sheets of any two structures have the same tangent spaces and dimensions (`exists_submanifoldTangent_eq`, `isOfDim_unique`); hence the footnote: an $n$-dimensional $\Theta$ with nonempty support is not $m$-dimensional for $m \ne n$ (`definition_9_1_2_footnote`, `_of_ne_zero`; for $\Theta = 0$ it does not hold as we read it, `definition_9_1_2_footnote_zero`). $\Theta$ is locally equidimensional if at every point of its support some local branching structure has sheets of one dimension; for branched $\Theta$ equivalently every local branching structure, restricted near the point, has sheets of that dimension (`IsLocallyEquidimensional`, `isLocallyEquidimensional_iff`), and the dimension is locally constant on the support (`exists_isOpen_isNDimensionalAt`). The hypothesis `HasLocallyConstantDimAt` and its proof on $\mathbb R^m$ are kept.

The footnote needs $\Theta \ne 0$: the zero functor is $n$-dimensional for every $n$, so for it the footnote does not hold as we read it (`definition_9_1_2_footnote_zero`). The dimension is measured in a chart, as in all of Chapter 9 (Findings, Chapter 9, items 2, 3, 107, 112). book.statement: A local branching structure on $U(x)$ restricts to $N_i = M_i \cap V(x_0)$ on $V(x_0) \subseteq U(x)$ with the same weights (some $N_i$ may be empty). items.title: Proposition 9.1.11 (2017: 9.2), the dimensional decomposition

book.label: §9.1, Proposition 9.1.11, pp. 407–408 (2017: Proposition 9.2, p. 297)
book.statement: A branched ep⁺-subgroupoid $\Theta$ determines a unique sequence $\Theta_0, \Theta_1, \ldots$ of branched ep⁺-subgroupoids characterized by (1) $\Theta_k$ is $k$-dimensional and (2) $\Theta = \Theta_0 + \Theta_1 + \cdots$, the sum locally finite. Proof: at $x \in \mathrm{supp}(\Theta)$ take a symmetric structure, split $I = I_0 \sqcup \cdots \sqcup I_n$ by the dimension of the $M_i$ and put $\Theta_k(y) = \sum_{i \in I_k, y \in M_i} \sigma_i$; independence of the structure is Proposition 9.1.12.

lean.statement: For a local branching structure with dimension labelling, $\Theta_k(y) = \sum_{\dim M_i = k,\, y \in M_i} \sigma_i$ is represented on $U(x)$ by the $k$-dimensional structure $(M_i)_{\dim M_i = k}$, $\Theta = \sum_k \Theta_k$ on $U(x)$, and for a symmetric structure $G_x$ preserves dimension and $\Theta_k$ is $G_x$-invariant. The statement of the proposition, \"a unique family $(\Theta_k)$ of branched ep⁺-subgroupoids, $\Theta_k$ $k$-dimensional, with $\Theta = \sum_k \Theta_k$ pointwise, and every such family locally finite\", is `Proposition_9_1_11`; on the trivial ep-groupoid of $\mathbb R^2$ it does not hold as we read it: for the indicator $\Theta$ of the $x$-axis $L$, both $\Theta_0 = 1_{\{0\}}$, $\Theta_1 = 1_{L \setminus \{0\}}$ and $\Theta_0 = 0$, $\Theta_1 = 1_L$ are such families. Uniqueness among local decompositions, those given near every point of $\mathrm{supp}(\Theta)$ by the dimensional parts of a local branching structure (the form the proof builds), for every ep-groupoid: `dimComponent`, the dimensional part of any labelled local branching structure, is a dimensional decomposition (`isDimDecomposition_dimComponent_general`), the only local one (`existsUnique_localDimDecomposition_general`, `proposition_9_1_11_unique`), and locally finite at the points of $\mathrm{supp}(\Theta)$ (`dimComponent_locallyFinite_of_mem_general`); `Proposition_9_1_11_local` (with local finiteness everywhere) holds under a bound on the dimensions of the submanifolds (`proposition_9_1_11_local_of_le`) and over $\mathbb R^m$ with no hypothesis (`proposition_9_1_11_local_rn`). In the example, $\Theta_1 = 1_L$ is local and the other decomposition is not. The forms first proved, under Proposition 9.1.12 and the local constancy of dimension, are kept (`proposition_9_1_11_local_of`, `proposition_9_1_11_unique_of_hasGraphChartAt`).

items.title: Example 9.3.5 (2017: 9.1)

book.statement: Four smooth $\beta^{\pm\pm}$ with graphs $G^{\pm\pm}$ define $\Theta$ in two ways; orienting by $\pm(1, 0)$ at the origin gives two orientations which coincide at $(0, 0)$ but are otherwise different; there are four possibilities to orient, and the second structure cannot necessarily be oriented to coincide with the first.
